questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Two pump blood to the gills, one pumps it to the rest of the body.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.fact: A group of owls is called a parliament.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's skin?
questions.fact: Black skin soaks up heat. The fur isn't white either, it's see-through.

questions.q: Which of these animals can't jump?
questions.fact: An elephant always keeps at least one foot on the ground.

questions.q: Which animal has fingerprints like ours?
questions.fact: Koala prints are so close to human ones they're hard to tell apart.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: So the Sun you see is about 8 minutes old.

questions.q: Which planet has the most moons?
questions.fact: Saturn has well over 200 known moons.

questions.q: What is the hottest planet?
questions.fact: Its thick clouds trap heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

questions.q: On Venus, which one is longer?
questions.fact: One Venus day is about 243 Earth days. Its year is about 225.

questions.q: How many bones does an adult have?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 300. Some fuse together as you grow.

questions.q: What is the largest organ in your body?
questions.fact: Your skin is constantly shedding and replacing itself.

questions.q: Which organ can regrow itself?
questions.fact: A liver can grow back even after a large part of it is removed.

questions.q: Where is the smallest bone in your body?
questions.fact: The stapes in your ear is about the size of a grain of rice.

questions.q: How many times does your heart beat a day?
questions.fact: That's over 35 million beats a year.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.fact: The Pacific is bigger than all the land on Earth combined.

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: What is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.fact: A desert is about low rainfall, not heat.

questions.q: Which country has the most islands?
questions.fact: Sweden has over 200,000 islands. Most have nobody living on them.

questions.q: Which country has the most time zones?
questions.fact: France has 12 thanks to its territories spread around the world.

questions.q: Which nut is used to make marzipan?
questions.fact: Marzipan is mostly ground almonds and sugar.

questions.q: Which of these is a berry?
questions.fact: Bananas count as berries. Strawberries and raspberries don't.

questions.q: Peanuts aren't nuts. What are they?
questions.fact: Peanuts are in the same family as beans and peas.

questions.q: Which food can last for thousands of years?
questions.fact: Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs.

questions.q: What color were carrots originally?
questions.fact: Orange carrots took off in the Netherlands in the 1600s.

questions.q: Which famous ship sank in 1912?
questions.fact: Titanic sank on her very first voyage.

questions.q: Which was invented first?
questions.fact: An early fax was patented in 1843, decades before the telephone.

questions.q: How long did the shortest war ever last?
questions.fact: That was the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896.

questions.q: Cleopatra lived closer in time to which event?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid was already about 2,500 years old when she was born.

questions.q: Oxford is older than which empire?
questions.fact: Oxford was teaching 200+ years before the Aztec capital existed.

questions.q: How many keys are on a standard piano?
questions.fact: 52 white keys and 36 black ones.

questions.q: What is the most spoken native language?
questions.fact: English is the most spoken overall once you count learners.

questions.q: Which letter isn't in any US state name?
questions.fact: Z is in Arizona and X is in Texas.

questions.q: What was the first toy advertised on TV?
questions.fact: Mr. Potato Head hit TV screens in 1952.

questions.q: Which sport has been played on the Moon?
questions.fact: Astronaut Alan Shepard hit two golf balls on the Moon in 1971.

questions.q: How many players start for each soccer team?
questions.fact: That includes the goalkeeper.

questions.q: How long is a marathon?
questions.fact: That's about 42.2 kilometers.

questions.q: Why do golf balls have dimples?
questions.fact: Dimples cut drag, so a ball can fly about twice as far.

questions.q: Which country has won the most World Cups?
questions.fact: Brazil has won the men's World Cup five times.

questions.q: What were the first basketball hoops?
questions.fact: Someone had to climb up and get the ball out after every basket.

questions.q: What is the largest animal alive today?
questions.fact: Its tongue alone can weigh as much as an elephant.

questions.q: How many arms does a starfish usually have?
questions.fact: One Antarctic starfish can grow up to 50 arms.

questions.q: How much of Earth is ocean?
questions.fact: We've seen less than 0.001% of the deep seafloor.
questions.fact_say: We've seen less than one thousandth of a percent of the deep seafloor.

questions.q: In which animal does the dad give birth?
questions.fact: Seahorse dads carry the eggs in a pouch until they hatch.

questions.q: How deep is the deepest part of the ocean?
questions.fact: Mount Everest would fit inside with about 2 kilometers to spare.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had three horns?
questions.fact: Its name means three-horned face.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had plates on its back?
questions.fact: Its name means roof lizard.

questions.q: Which animals are living dinosaurs?
questions.fact: Birds evolved from small feathered dinosaurs.

questions.q: T. rex lived closer in time to whom?
questions.fact: Stegosaurus vanished about 80 million years before T. rex.
questions.q_say: Tyrannosaurus rex lived closer in time to whom?
questions.fact_say: Stegosaurus vanished about eighty million years before Tyrannosaurus rex.

questions.q: What is fossil dinosaur poop called?
questions.fact: Scientists study it to learn what dinosaurs ate.

questions.q: Which tool always points north?
questions.fact: Compasses were first used in ancient China.

questions.q: What did the Wright brothers build?
questions.fact: Their first flight in 1903 lasted 12 seconds.
questions.fact_say: Their first flight in nineteen oh three lasted twelve seconds.

questions.q: A candy bar led to which invention?
questions.fact: A melted candy bar gave an engineer the idea.

questions.q: What was the first item scanned by barcode?
questions.fact: A pack of gum was scanned in Ohio in 1974.
questions.fact_say: A pack of gum was scanned in Ohio in nineteen seventy four.

questions.q: How old was the Popsicle's inventor?
questions.fact: He left soda with a stick outside on a cold night.

questions.q: What falls from storms as balls of ice?
questions.fact: Some hailstones grow as big as softballs.

questions.q: What is the middle of a hurricane called?
questions.fact: The eye is calm, but the winds around it are fierce.

questions.q: Is lightning hotter than the Sun's surface?
questions.fact: A bolt can reach about 50,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
questions.fact_say: A bolt can reach about fifty thousand degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Which cloud word means rain?
questions.fact: Nimbus is Latin for rain. Cumulus means heap.

questions.q: Where do Celsius and Fahrenheit match?
questions.fact: At minus 40, both scales show the same number.
questions.fact_say: At minus forty, both scales show the same number.

questions.q: How many strings does a guitar have?
questions.fact: A bass guitar usually has just four.
questions.q_say: How many strings does a standard guitar have?

questions.q: A trumpet belongs to which family?
questions.fact: Brass players make sound by buzzing their lips.

questions.q: A Stradivarius is what instrument?
questions.fact: Antonio Stradivari made them in Italy around 1700.
questions.fact_say: Antonio Stradivari made them in Italy around seventeen hundred.

questions.q: Which composer kept writing while deaf?
questions.fact: Beethoven kept composing even as he lost his hearing.

questions.q: The oldest instruments ever found are?
questions.fact: Bone flutes over 40,000 years old were found in Germany.
questions.fact_say: Bone flutes over forty thousand years old were found in Germany.

questions.q: Whose nose grows when he lies?
questions.fact: Pinocchio is a wooden puppet who wants to be a real boy.

questions.q: What does Simba mean in Swahili?
questions.fact: Rafiki, the wise baboon, is Swahili for friend.

questions.q: What is an Oscar statue made of?
questions.fact: It stands 13.5 inches tall and weighs 8.5 pounds.
questions.fact_say: It stands thirteen and a half inches tall and weighs eight and a half pounds.

questions.q: What made Toy Story a first in 1995?
questions.fact: It was the first full-length film made entirely on computers.

questions.q: Which animal is in the T. rex roar?
questions.fact: Sound designers mixed elephant, tiger and alligator noises.
questions.q_say: Which animal's sound is in the Jurassic Park T. rex roar?

questions.q: Which letter is used most in English?
questions.fact: About one in eight letters in English text is an E.

questions.q: Racecar is an example of a what?
questions.fact: A palindrome reads the same forward and backward.

questions.q: How many letters does Hawaiian have?
questions.fact: Hawaiian uses just 13 letters, including five vowels.

questions.q: What is the most used word in English?
questions.fact: Ten tiny words make up about a quarter of English.

questions.q: About how many languages exist today?
questions.fact: Papua New Guinea alone has over 800 of them.

questions.q: What was the first computer mouse made of?
questions.fact: Douglas Engelbart's 1964 prototype had a wooden shell.
questions.fact_say: Douglas Engelbart's nineteen sixty four prototype had a wooden shell.

questions.q: The first computer bug was a real what?
questions.fact: It was taped into a Harvard logbook in 1947.
questions.fact_say: It was taped into a Harvard logbook in nineteen forty seven.

questions.q: What does Wi-Fi stand for?
questions.fact: A marketing company made up the name Wi-Fi.

questions.q: What did the first text message say?
questions.fact: It was sent in 1992 from a computer to a phone.
questions.fact_say: It was sent in nineteen ninety two from a computer to a phone.

questions.q: What was the first message sent online?
questions.fact: The system crashed after two letters of login.

questions.q: Blue plus yellow makes which color?
questions.fact: Red plus blue makes purple.

questions.q: What do painters mix colors on?
questions.fact: Many palettes have a thumb hole to hold them.

questions.q: Which artist painted melting clocks?
questions.fact: The painting is called The Persistence of Memory.

questions.q: What metal is the Statue of Liberty's skin?
questions.fact: Its copper skin slowly turned green with age.
questions.q_say: What metal is the skin of the Statue of Liberty?

questions.q: How tall is the Mona Lisa painting?
questions.fact: It's smaller than many people expect.
questions.answer_say: about two and a half feet

questions.q: Which mountain is tallest above sea level?
questions.fact: Everest stands about 29,000 feet high.
questions.fact_say: Everest stands about twenty nine thousand feet high.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.fact: Cheetahs can run over 60 miles per hour.
questions.fact_say: Cheetahs can run over sixty miles per hour.

questions.q: What is the largest rainforest on Earth?
questions.fact: It stretches across nine countries.

questions.q: Which country is largest by area?
questions.fact: Russia spans 11 time zones.

questions.q: Which animal is fastest on Earth?
questions.fact: In a dive, it tops 200 miles per hour.
questions.fact_say: In a dive, it tops two hundred miles per hour.

questions.q: Which is the largest US state?
questions.fact: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.q: Which is the smallest US state?
questions.fact: Rhode Island is only about 48 miles long.
questions.fact_say: Rhode Island is only about forty eight miles long.

questions.q: Which US state is entirely islands?
questions.fact: Hawaii has eight main islands and over 100 small ones.
questions.fact_say: Hawaii has eight main islands and over one hundred small ones.

questions.q: Which state has a town called Boring?
questions.fact: Boring, Oregon is a sister town of Dull, Scotland.

questions.q: Which state's flag isn't a rectangle?
questions.fact: Ohio's flag is shaped like a pointed swallowtail.
